questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: First of all, I wanted to go an English-speaking country. I also wanted to go outside of Europe, and I have always wanted to go to Australia. I had heard really good things about Melbourne and UniMelb from previous students, which is why my choice ended on Melbourne.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I don't really remember any big issues, so it was probably pretty straight forward to find most of the information needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: UniMelb offered free transportation from the airport to your desired address in Melbourne. You just had to sign up (I think it was 48 hours) before the pick up.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I ended up living with another danish girl from KU who already had found an apartment Melbourne, but needed a roommate. 
I met her in Copenhagen where all of us who had been accepted to UniMelb met up. So I highly recommend attending in meet-ups like that, also so you have a chance to meet some new people before arriving.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is usually cheaper to live off campus, but also harder to find a place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Pretty straight forward. The registration website was running really slow so it took forever, but other than that, pretty easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not really sure, didn't really use any help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up getting all the classes I wanted. If one of your classes is full, you can just keep an eye on it, since people back out/change their classes before the semester starts.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do it at some point where you have plenty of time for it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two level 1 courses and two level 3 courses. I found the level 3 classes to be a little bit easier the than level of KU courses. The level 1 courses was pretty easy too.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The courses consist of lectures, classes and practicals like they also do at KU. 
The exams are broken up into different assessments during the semester, which all count towards your grade, instead of having one final exam. 
Also UniMelb records all of the lectures, so you can either watch them live from home or watch them later. Really nice if you want to go on weekend trips or if you have overlapping courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Developmental Neurobiology (NEUR30005)
Stem Cells in Development & Regeneration (CEDB30004)
The History of Cool: Fashion & Attitude (DPSS10007)
Australia in the Wine World (AGRI10039)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed and would recommend all of my courses.
Developmental Neurobiology was pretty straight forward and not so electrochemistry heavy, but more biology focused which was really nice. I found it very interesting and learned a lot from it.  
Stem cells was really cool, where we learned a lot about the current techniques and where we are in the field today. Some stuff also overlapped with what I had learned in developmental neurobiology, so the two courses went pretty good together. 
The history of cool is a really fun subject, and something completely different from what I'm used to. It is an online course, but it only has one lecture + one tutorial a week, so it was not an issue for me. Very easy course, and it does not have a final exam (you just hand in a final assignment). That was super nice, so I had more time to focus on studying for the exams for the other subjects. 
Australia in the Wine World was also super fun. You do have to put in a little bit of work, and show up for the lectures/pracs, but it was really fun to have a winetasting once a week, and I really learned a lot about wine which is such a nice skill to have.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Don't really think I had any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Groceries is pretty expensive. 
Eating out is a bit cheaper than in Copenhagen, and coffee especially is very cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: UniMelb has a lot of different clubs and societies. I joined the athletics club which uses the track on campus. There is also a gym on campus which is super nice and convenient.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on weekend trips to different parts of Australia. The country has so much to offer and so much to do.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went to Kangaroo Island, Tasmania, Sydney and also drove the Great Ocean Road. I also spend a little over a month on the West Coast after the semester ended, which I highly recommend!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Melbourne is pretty similar to Copenhagen, so it was pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Since the lectures at uni is being recorded, not so many people show up for them, so I found it a bit difficult to socialize with local students. However I met a lot through the track team, so I recommend signing up for clubs instead.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Can't remember any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The open-minded and helpful attitude everyone has. People are much easier to approach here than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it and be prepared to spend a lot of money.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I bought a bike to get around the city. Much easier than the tram system.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I met down here. Since you really only have each other, you get really close in a short period of time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To find time to do all I wanted to do here. Could easily have spend a year here!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
